paper.title: Accurate prediction of tensorial spectra using equivariant graph neural network
paper.research_summary: Here we introduce the Tensorial Spectra Equivariant Neural Network (TSENN), an equivariant graph neural network architecture that maps crystal structures directly to their full photon-frequency-dependent optical tensors. By encoding isotropic sequential scalar components and anisotropic sequential tensor components into spherical tensor representations, TSENN ensures symmetry-aware predictions consistent with crystalline symmetry constraints. Trained on frequency-dependent dielectric tensors of 1,432 bulk semiconductors, the model achieves a mean absolute error of 0.127, demonstrating its potential for efficient and general modeling of optical properties.

task.objective: map crystal structures directly to their full photon-frequency-dependent optical tensors

evidence.text: Here we introduce the Tensorial Spectra Equivariant Neural Network (TSENN), an equivariant graph neural network architecture that maps crystal structures directly to their full photon-frequency-dependent optical tensors.

stages.stage_name_raw: ab initio calculations of dielectric tensors
stages.stage_goal: compute frequency-dependent dielectric tensors for 1432 bulk semiconductors using first-principles methods

evidence.text: By training TSENN on the aforementioned dataset, we achieve a mean absolute error (MAE) of 0.127 in the predicted imaginary part of the dielectric tensor.

For each entry, we first symmetrized the structure by following the procedure of ref. 44 and performed first-principles calculations using OpenMX. The dielectric tensors were computed using the Kubo formula for photon energies ranging from 0 to 30 eV, with an increment of 0.01 eV, resulting in 1432 frequency-dependent dielectric tensors satisfying the symmetry constraints of the crystal systems considered.

stages.stage_goal: transform Cartesian dielectric tensors into spherical-harmonics basis to encode rotational symmetry

evidence.text: To predict the dielectric tensor using an equivariant neural network, we express it in the spherical-harmonics basis, which naturally encodes rotational symmetry.

The dielectric tensor is symmetric under the permutation of Cartesian indices, εij = εji, and therefore admits the decomposition εij = Tαβ Y α 1 Y β 1 = ε(0)  ε(2) = ∑ ‘2f0, 2g ∑ ‘ m = ‘ εm (‘) Y m ‘ , (1) which separates the scalar trace component (ℓ= 0) from the traceless symmetric tensor component (ℓ= 2).

stages.stage_goal: train equivariant graph neural network to predict ℓ=0 and ℓ=2 spherical-harmonics components from crystal graphs

evidence.text: Our TSENN model extends the e3nn and GNNOpt frameworks... TSENN leverages higher-order spherical-harmonic components to better capture the anisotropy of tensorial properties.
To train the model, we define a composite loss function L, which separately evaluates the scalar and tensor components of the predicted optical spectra.

stages.stage_name_raw: evaluation of dielectric tensor prediction accuracy
stages.stage_goal: quantify prediction errors using MAE and other metrics on full-tensor and per-component levels

evidence.text: To evaluate the model’s performance, the most direct measure is the MAE of the dielectric tensor, MAE = 1 6nω ∑ ω ∑ α ≤β |bε αβ(ω) − εαβ(ω)|.

stages.stage_goal: reconstruct real parts of dielectric tensor from predicted imaginary parts and validate symmetry preservation

evidence.text: With the accurately predicted imaginary parts, we used K–K relations to obtain the real parts of the dielectric tensors.
To further confirm symmetry preservation, we applied a symmetry-based masking procedure to the predicted tensor at each photon energy.
